claims.claim: The listed defenses are common in consumer debt lawsuits.
The debt can be too old to sue on.
claims.quote: When the period in which an action must be commenced under this section has run, a person shall not bring suit or initiate an arbitration or other legal proceeding to collect the debt.
claims.note: Supported as a possible defense for debts covered by this section, not as a finding about any particular debt.

claims.claim: The plaintiff's inability to show it owns the debt is a defense.
claims.note: No supplied text establishes what the plaintiff must prove about ownership.

claims.claim: The plaintiff's inability to show the amount of the debt is a defense.
claims.note: No supplied text addresses proof of the amount owed.

claims.claim: That the debt is not yours is a defense.
claims.quote: (1) The general or specific denial of the material allegations of the complaint controverted by the defendant.
claims.note: This supports denying an allegation that the defendant owes the debt. It does not identify mistaken identity as a separate defense.
No supplied text addresses service or how to challenge it.

claims.claim: A defense that is not raised can be lost.
claims.quote: (2) A statement of any new matter constituting a defense.
claims.note: Section 431.30(b) requires this statement in the answer but does not say when omission results in loss of a defense.

claims.claim: Read the response form before filing.
claims.note: The form is named but was not supplied; its instructions cannot be checked.
No supplied text gives this instruction.

flags.text: “Common ones” asserts frequency without support and groups denials, defenses, and a service challenge together without distinguishing how each is raised.
The sources do not establish the ownership, amount, or service claims, or the consequence of omitting a defense. PLD-050 item 2 was not supplied.
Linking improper service to the response form may imply that putting a service objection on that form preserves it. The supplied sources do not establish that.
“Read the response form and ask for help before you file” directly instructs the reader.

result.summary: Section 337 supports a possible time bar for covered debts. Section 431.30 addresses denials and pleading defenses, but does not verify the full list or the warning about losing a defense.
